scope: Public instruction and bounded input previews from existing generated Harbor tasks. No private answers, solver traces or benchmark fixtures. These are frozen examples, not a new corpus build.

examples.instruction:
Analyze the unchanged NC_001422.1 genome and deposited coding annotations in /app/inputs. Read operation parameters and genome topology from query.json. GFF3 coordinates are 1-based inclusive; repeated CDS IDs are parts of one coding sequence. The part=i/n attribute specifies biological 5'-to-3' concatenation order, including origin-crossing or overlapping parts. Orient each part by its strand before concatenating; do not discard phase bases from later parts. All supplied CDSs are complete and reproduce deposited proteins. Report each complete coding sequence and its length, keyed by the CDS ID.

Write /app/answer.json as a JSON array of records, with one record per requested id.
Each record must contain a string id and exactly the fields below. Record order is irrelevant.
Do not duplicate or omit IDs. Extra IDs/fields, booleans as numbers, and nonfinite numbers fail.
- sequence: text (DNA); complete oriented CDS including stop codon.
- length: integer (bases); CDS length.
Numeric tolerance is abs(actual - reference) <= atol + rtol * abs(reference).
examples.derivation: Full reference genome unchanged; complete CDS coordinates converted from deposited GenBank to GFF3. Biopython 1.86 extraction/translation checked against deposited proteins; all retained parts and exclusions are recorded in the source preparation. Instance query selects the declared operation and window size.

examples.instruction:
Analyze the observed GSE60450 mouse mammary-gland RNA-seq experiment. Join samples.tsv to counts.tsv by sample ID. The matrix has 27,179 Entrez genes and twelve libraries; Length is an annotation column. Select query.json's cell population and retain its six libraries, two biological replicates at each of virgin, 18.5 days pregnant and 2 days lactating. Preserve the counts. Filter genes to total count >=10 across all six selected libraries. Fit DESeq2 1.50.2 design ~stage with stage levels virgin, '18.5 dP', '2 dL', ratio size factors, parametric dispersion, Wald tests, betaPrior=FALSE and no count replacement. Keep all three stages in the fit; extract treatment relative to baseline from query.json. Disable Cook's filtering and independent filtering; use BH adjustment over all retained genes, with no effect shrinkage. Write sample_qc.tsv for every selected library and de_results.tsv for every retained gene, including missing test results. QC totals/detected genes use the full unfiltered matrix; size factors use the filtered model. Probability fields are -log10(max(p,1e-300)), preserving NA. Use the specified inclusive FDR and absolute log2-effect cutoffs to identify up/downregulated genes. All inputs are in /app/inputs. Continue the fitted contrast into GO biological-process over-representation analysis using the frozen propagated memberships in go_membership.tsv; go_terms.tsv gives term names. The universe is finite-tested genes with any supplied BP annotation. Select the significant direction in query.json and intersect it with that universe. Restrict each term to the universe; test every term with 10..500 universe genes, including zero-overlap terms. Use the upper-tail hypergeometric probability P(X>=observed overlap), then BH across all eligible terms. Write enrichment.tsv for every tested term. Return the report_terms smallest raw probabilities, breaking ties lexicographically by GO ID, with the GO ID as id. Interpret this as association in a selected gene set, without claiming pathway activation or a causal effect. 

Write /app/answer.json as a JSON array of records, with one record per requested id.
Each record must contain a string id and exactly the fields below. Record order is irrelevant.
Do not duplicate or omit IDs. Extra IDs/fields, booleans as numbers, and nonfinite numbers fail.
- overlap: integer (genes); selected genes in this term.
- term_size: integer (genes); term genes in declared universe.
- selected_genes: integer (genes); selected DE genes in declared universe.
- background_genes: integer (genes); finite tested genes with BP annotation.
- neg_log10_p: number (log probability); upper-tail hypergeometric probability as capped -log10; absolute tolerance 1e-05, relative tolerance 1e-06.
- neg_log10_padj: number (log probability); BH probability across all eligible terms as capped -log10; absolute tolerance 1e-05, relative tolerance 1e-06.
Numeric tolerance is abs(actual - reference) <= atol + rtol * abs(reference).
Also write /app/sample_qc.tsv as UTF-8 TSV, with an id column and exactly these columns: library_counts, detected_genes, size_factor. Row and column order are irrelevant; duplicate, missing and extra IDs fail. Use NA for specified missing values. Fields must occupy one line. Every row is verified; a correct JSON summary alone does not pass.
- sample_qc.tsv.library_counts: integer (counts); all observed counts before gene filtering; absolute tolerance 0.0, relative tolerance 0.0.
- sample_qc.tsv.detected_genes: integer (genes); positive-count genes before filtering; absolute tolerance 0.0, relative tolerance 0.0.
- sample_qc.tsv.size_factor: number (factor); DESeq2 ratio size factor on the filtered model matrix; absolute tolerance 1e-05, relative tolerance 1e-06.
Also write /app/de_results.tsv as UTF-8 TSV, with an id column and exactly these columns: base_mean, log2_fold_change, standard_error, wald_statistic, neg_log10_p, neg_log10_padj. Row and column order are irrelevant; duplicate, missing and extra IDs fail. Use NA for specified missing values. Fields must occupy one line. Every row is verified; a correct JSON summary alone does not pass.
- de_results.tsv.base_mean: number (counts); mean of normalized counts in all six modeled samples; absolute tolerance 1e-05, relative tolerance 1e-06.
- de_results.tsv.log2_fold_change: number (log2); unshrunk treatment relative to baseline effect; absolute tolerance 1e-05, relative tolerance 1e-06.
- de_results.tsv.standard_error: number (log2); unshrunk effect standard error; absolute tolerance 1e-05, relative tolerance 1e-06.
- de_results.tsv.wald_statistic: number (statistic); Wald coefficient divided by standard error; absolute tolerance 1e-05, relative tolerance 1e-06.
- de_results.tsv.neg_log10_p: number (log probability); negative log10 raw probability, capped at 300; absolute tolerance 1e-05, relative tolerance 1e-06.
- de_results.tsv.neg_log10_padj: number (log probability); negative log10 BH probability, capped at 300; absolute tolerance 1e-05, relative tolerance 1e-06.
Also write /app/enrichment.tsv as UTF-8 TSV, with an id column and exactly these columns: overlap, term_size, selected_genes, background_genes, neg_log10_p, neg_log10_padj. Row and column order are irrelevant; duplicate, missing and extra IDs fail. Use NA for specified missing values. Fields must occupy one line. Every row is verified; a correct JSON summary alone does not pass.
- enrichment.tsv.overlap: integer (genes); selected genes in this term; absolute tolerance 0.0, relative tolerance 0.0.
- enrichment.tsv.term_size: integer (genes); term genes in declared universe; absolute tolerance 0.0, relative tolerance 0.0.
- enrichment.tsv.selected_genes: integer (genes); selected DE genes in declared universe; absolute tolerance 0.0, relative tolerance 0.0.
- enrichment.tsv.background_genes: integer (genes); finite tested genes with BP annotation; absolute tolerance 0.0, relative tolerance 0.0.
- enrichment.tsv.neg_log10_p: number (log probability); upper-tail hypergeometric probability as capped -log10; absolute tolerance 1e-05, relative tolerance 1e-06.
- enrichment.tsv.neg_log10_padj: number (log probability); BH probability across all eligible terms as capped -log10; absolute tolerance 1e-05, relative tolerance 1e-06.

examples.instruction:
Prepare an auditable filtered count matrix for the observed mouse hematopoietic stem/progenitor Smart-seq2 study GSE81682. All inputs are in /app/inputs. matrix.mtx.gz is a gzip-compressed Matrix Market coordinate integer general matrix with features as rows and cells as columns. features.tsv and cells.tsv list those identities in matrix order. Counts are aligned reads. Use feature_type to distinguish endogenous genes from ERCC spike-ins; the __ columns in cell metadata are HTSeq alignment summaries and are excluded from gene counts. Apply the explicit analysis policy in query.json to every supplied cell: require endogenous read counts >= minimum_endogenous_counts, detected endogenous genes >= minimum_detected_endogenous, and ERCC/all-count fraction <= ercc_fraction_numerator / ercc_fraction_denominator. All counts means endogenous plus ERCC counts. Detected means a strictly positive count. Compute QC on the original matrix before gene filtering. An empty cell has a null ERCC fraction and fails the positive count requirements. Write cell_qc.tsv for every original cell, preserving its GEO accession and broad sorting gate, with the stated metrics, keep indicator and output matrix_column. Excluded cells have matrix_column=0; retained cells receive contiguous 1-based indices in original order. After cell selection, count retained cells and read counts for every original feature. Retain endogenous genes observed in at least minimum_retained_cells_per_gene retained cells, and exclude ERCC rows from the final matrix. Write feature_qc.tsv for all original features, including ERCC, with feature_type, retained_cell_count, retained_read_count, keep and matrix_row. Excluded features have matrix_row=0; retained features receive contiguous 1-based indices in original order. Export filtered_counts.mtx.gz with all retained integer counts, features as rows and cells as columns, and report the study totals in answer.json. Use these descriptive QC criteria as specified; they are not the original authors' final cell selection or universal biological cutoffs. Broad sorting gates do not supply donor identities or fine cell annotations. Do not infer mitochondrial, donor or cell-type labels.

Write /app/answer.json as a JSON array of records, with one record per requested id.
Each record must contain a string id and exactly the fields below. Record order is irrelevant.
Do not duplicate or omit IDs. Extra IDs/fields, booleans as numbers, and nonfinite numbers fail.
- input_cells: integer (cells); number of supplied cell columns.
- retained_cells: integer (cells); cells passing all stated filters.
- input_features: integer (features); supplied endogenous and ERCC rows.
- retained_features: integer (genes); endogenous genes passing the post-cell-QC filter.
- output_nonzeros: integer (entries); positive counts in the exported matrix.
- output_read_counts: integer (read counts); sum of exported integer counts.
Numeric tolerance is abs(actual - reference) <= atol + rtol * abs(reference).
Also write /app/cell_qc.tsv as UTF-8 TSV, with an id column and exactly these columns: geo_accession, sorting_gate, all_counts, ercc_counts, endogenous_counts, detected_endogenous, keep, matrix_column, ercc_fraction. Row and column order are irrelevant; duplicate, missing and extra IDs fail. Use NA for specified missing values. Fields must occupy one line. Every row is verified; a correct JSON summary alone does not pass.
- cell_qc.tsv.geo_accession: text (accession); source GEO sample; absolute tolerance 0.0, relative tolerance 0.0.
- cell_qc.tsv.sorting_gate: text (label); supplied broad sorting gate; absolute tolerance 0.0, relative tolerance 0.0.
- cell_qc.tsv.all_counts: integer (read counts); endogenous plus ERCC counts before filtering; absolute tolerance 0.0, relative tolerance 0.0.
- cell_qc.tsv.ercc_counts: integer (read counts); ERCC counts before filtering; absolute tolerance 0.0, relative tolerance 0.0.
- cell_qc.tsv.endogenous_counts: integer (read counts); endogenous counts before filtering; absolute tolerance 0.0, relative tolerance 0.0.
- cell_qc.tsv.detected_endogenous: integer (genes); endogenous genes with positive counts before filtering; absolute tolerance 0.0, relative tolerance 0.0.
- cell_qc.tsv.keep: integer (indicator); one if all cell criteria pass, zero otherwise; absolute tolerance 0.0, relative tolerance 0.0.
- cell_qc.tsv.matrix_column: integer (1-based index); output column in original cell order, or zero if excluded; absolute tolerance 0.0, relative tolerance 0.0.
- cell_qc.tsv.ercc_fraction: number (fraction); ERCC divided by all counts, null for an empty cell; absolute tolerance 1e-12, relative tolerance 1e-09.
Also write /app/feature_qc.tsv as UTF-8 TSV, with an id column and exactly these columns: feature_type, retained_cell_count, retained_read_count, keep, matrix_row. Row and column order are irrelevant; duplicate, missing and extra IDs fail. Use NA for specified missing values. Fields must occupy one line. Every row is verified; a correct JSON summary alone does not pass.
- feature_qc.tsv.feature_type: text (label); endogenous or ERCC; absolute tolerance 0.0, relative tolerance 0.0.
- feature_qc.tsv.retained_cell_count: integer (cells); QC-passing cells with a positive count for this feature; absolute tolerance 0.0, relative tolerance 0.0.
- feature_qc.tsv.retained_read_count: integer (read counts); sum of this feature across QC-passing cells; absolute tolerance 0.0, relative tolerance 0.0.
- feature_qc.tsv.keep: integer (indicator); one if endogenous and present in enough retained cells; absolute tolerance 0.0, relative tolerance 0.0.
- feature_qc.tsv.matrix_row: integer (1-based index); output row in original feature order, or zero if excluded; absolute tolerance 0.0, relative tolerance 0.0.
Also write /app/filtered_counts.mtx.gz as MatrixMarket coordinate integer general, with 40312 rows, 1422 columns and 17332418 positive entries. Use one 1-based coordinate per nonzero count, with no duplicate coordinates or explicit zeros. Every count and coordinate is checked; entry order, whitespace and comments are ignored. Use gzip compression for a .gz filename. Integer counts must be below 2^63. The file must be at most 134217728 bytes, at most 536870912 decoded bytes, and at most 65536 bytes per line. A correct JSON summary alone does not pass.
examples.derivation: All 1,920 original cells, 46,078 endogenous features and 92 ERCC rows; unchanged counts, original identities and ordering. Scanpy reference and independent streaming oracle agree on all cell/feature tables and 17,332,418 filtered matrix entries.

examples.instruction:
Analyze the unchanged experimental structure 1CRN in /app/inputs/structure.cif. Use only model 1, ATOM records, and protein alpha carbons (auth_atom_id CA). Identify residues by auth_asym_id, auth_seq_id, and pdbx_PDB_ins_code; '.' and '?' mean no insertion code. For alternate conformers, retain highest occupancy; ties use lexicographically smallest label_alt_id with '.' or '?' treated as empty. Coordinates and distances are in angstroms. For each author chain, report its CA centroid, unweighted radius of gyration about that centroid, and residue count.

Write /app/answer.json as a JSON array of records, with one record per requested id.
Each record must contain a string id and exactly the fields below. Record order is irrelevant.
Do not duplicate or omit IDs. Extra IDs/fields, booleans as numbers, and nonfinite numbers fail.
- x: number (angstrom); CA centroid x coordinate; absolute tolerance 1e-07, relative tolerance 1e-09.
- y: number (angstrom); CA centroid y coordinate; absolute tolerance 1e-07, relative tolerance 1e-09.
- z: number (angstrom); CA centroid z coordinate; absolute tolerance 1e-07, relative tolerance 1e-09.
- radius: number (angstrom); unweighted CA radius of gyration; absolute tolerance 1e-07, relative tolerance 1e-09.
- n_residues: integer (residues); selected alpha carbons.
Numeric tolerance is abs(actual - reference) <= atol + rtol * abs(reference).

examples.instruction:
Assemble the supplied observed PhiX paired reads and assess contiguity and agreement with the deposited reference genome. Inputs are in /app/inputs. The FASTQs are systematically spaced records across the full ENA ERR266411 run, with original sequences, qualities and matching mate identifiers. This technical subset is not biological replication. First report complete per-mate read and quality counts in read_qc.tsv, with ids R1 and R2. Use all input reads unchanged. Run the installed SPAdes with --isolate --only-assembler, the k-mer lengths in query.json, one thread and a 4 GB memory limit. Retain every native contig and its identifier in contigs.fa; use contigs.fasta rather than scaffolds. Align these contigs to reference.fa with minimap2 -x asm5 --secondary=no --eqx -c --cs=long -t 1. Include every reported alignment, including split alignments, in alignments.tsv. Use id=contig:strand:query_start:query_end:reference_start:reference_end. Coordinates are zero-based and half-open; query coordinates refer to the original forward contig. Write contig_metrics.tsv keyed by native contig ID and reference_coverage.tsv keyed by reference_id:zero_based_position for every reference position, including zeros. Count contig depth only where a query base is paired to a reference base (= or X); insertions and deletions do not contribute. Within each contig, count aligned query positions once when alignments overlap. Sum matches and errors over alignments without that deduplication. Write answer.json for id=assembly with complete input, assembly and reference accounting. For N50/L50 and NG50/LG50, sort all contig lengths descending and include the first contig reaching at least half the relevant length; do not filter short contigs. NG50/LG50 use the reference length and are null if the threshold is never reached. The reference is circular, but this task measures the native linear contigs and alignments without circularization or reference-guided correction. Contig-alignment breadth describes reference agreement; it is not read depth or a guarantee of assembly correctness.

Write /app/answer.json as a JSON array of records, with one record per requested id.
Each record must contain a string id and exactly the fields below. Record order is irrelevant.
Do not duplicate or omit IDs. Extra IDs/fields, booleans as numbers, and nonfinite numbers fail.
- read_pairs: integer (pairs); all observed input read pairs.
- input_bases: integer (bases); sum of both mates' sequence lengths.
- contigs: integer (contigs); all native contigs, including unaligned contigs.
- assembled_bases: integer (bases); sum of complete contig lengths.
- reference_length: integer (bases); complete supplied reference length.
- n50: integer (bases); contig length crossing half the assembled length.
- l50: integer (contigs); number of descending-length contigs needed to cross half the assembled length.
- ng50: integer (bases); contig length crossing half the reference length; null if never reached; use null when specified.
- lg50: integer (contigs); number needed to cross half the reference length; null if never reached; use null when specified.
- aligned_contigs: integer (contigs); contigs with at least one reported reference alignment.
- reference_covered_bases: integer (bases); reference positions paired to at least one query base.
- reference_uncovered_bases: integer (bases); reference positions with zero aligned contig depth.
- multiply_covered_reference_bases: integer (bases); reference positions paired to at least two query bases.
- aligned_query_bases: integer (bases); union of matched or substituted query positions within each contig.
- matches: integer (aligned bases); sum of exact matches over all reported alignments.
- substitutions: integer (aligned bases); sum of nucleotide substitutions over all reported alignments.
- inserted_bases: integer (bases); query insertions over all reported alignments.
- deleted_bases: integer (bases); reference deletions over all reported alignments.
Numeric tolerance is abs(actual - reference) <= atol + rtol * abs(reference).
Also write /app/contigs.fa as unaligned FASTA, at most 1048576 bytes. Every requested first-token ID and its complete sequence must occur exactly once. Record order, letter case, line wrapping, blank lines and header comments are ignored. Do not add gaps or change residues. Every sequence is verified; a correct JSON summary alone does not pass.
Also write /app/read_qc.tsv as UTF-8 TSV, with an id column and exactly these columns: reads, bases, q20_bases, q30_bases, n_bases. Row and column order are irrelevant; duplicate, missing and extra IDs fail. Use NA for specified missing values. Fields must occupy one line. Every row is verified; a correct JSON summary alone does not pass.
- read_qc.tsv.reads: integer (reads); records for this mate; absolute tolerance 0.0, relative tolerance 0.0.
- read_qc.tsv.bases: integer (bases); complete input bases; absolute tolerance 0.0, relative tolerance 0.0.
- read_qc.tsv.q20_bases: integer (bases); Phred+33 quality at least 20; absolute tolerance 0.0, relative tolerance 0.0.

examples.instruction:
Audit the lactation-associated expression response in luminal mammary cells from GSE60450. The two requested enrichment specifications reflect different analysis choices. Determine their gene/term selections and quantify how coefficient shrinkage changes the absolute-effect threshold. Inputs are in /app/inputs. Join samples.tsv to counts.tsv by sample ID; Length is annotation. Use all six luminal libraries, with two biological replicates at each stage. Do not infer donor pairing. Retain genes with count sum >=10 across those libraries. Use DESeq2 1.50.2, design ~stage, levels virgin, '18.5 dP', '2 dL', ratio size factors, parametric dispersions, Wald tests, betaPrior=FALSE, and no count replacement. Keep pregnant libraries in the fit. Extract the named stage_2.dL_vs_virgin coefficient (not the character contrast interface, which resets genes zero in both compared stages), using alpha=.05, BH adjustment, independentFiltering=TRUE and cooksCutoff=TRUE. Apply apeglm 1.32.0 shrinkage to that coefficient with apeMethod=nbinomCR and the same Wald result. Preserve original p-values, BH values and Wald statistics; do not derive significance from shrunken effects. Write sample_qc.tsv using unfiltered library totals/detected genes and fitted size factors; gene_results.tsv for every fitted gene; and gene_decisions.tsv for all 27,179 input genes. Raw/adjusted significance is finite p/padj <.05; large_shrunken_effect means finite absolute shrunken log2FC >=1 regardless of significance. Excluded genes receive zero membership indicators. All probability fields are -log10(max(p,1e-300)); preserve NA model values. Use the installed org.Mm.eg.db 3.22.0 and GO.db 3.22.0, propagated GOALL biological-process memberships whose IDs are valid BP terms in GO.db. adjusted_tested selects adjusted-significant genes and uses finite-raw-p genes as background; raw_genome selects raw-significant genes and uses all genes in the annotation database with valid BP annotation as background. Intersect each selection/background with annotated genes before testing. Neither ORA selection includes an effect-size or directional cutoff. Write annotation_membership.tsv for every annotated gene, including genes absent from the count matrix. For each specification run clusterProfiler 4.18.4 enrichGO, keyType=ENTREZID, ont=BP, readable=FALSE, BH, minGSSize=10, maxGSSize=500, pvalueCutoff=qvalueCutoff=1; set seed 42 before each call. Export its complete @result hypothesis family to the corresponding enrichment table: size-eligible terms with nonzero selected overlap. Preserve the native BH denominator; do not append zero-overlap terms or apply Storey-qvalue filtering. Term significance is p.adjust <.05. Return an answer.json array containing one object with id=audit and all eight summary fields. changed_effect_threshold counts fitted genes whose absolute effect >=1 status differs between raw and shrunken coefficients. The two ORA specifications change selection and background jointly, so their difference cannot isolate one cause. Enrichment does not establish pathway activation or causal developmental effects.

Write /app/answer.json as a JSON array of records, with one record per requested id.
Each record must contain a string id and exactly the fields below. Record order is irrelevant.
All fields belong together in each record; field names are not separate record IDs.
Do not duplicate or omit IDs. Extra IDs/fields, booleans as numbers, and nonfinite numbers fail.
Example of one record in the array: repeat the record for every requested ID. Replace all angle-bracket placeholders with the requested IDs and computed values.
```json
[
  {
    "id": "<requested record id>",
    "genes_fitted": "<integer>",
    "raw_significant": "<integer>",
    "adjusted_significant": "<integer>",
    "large_shrunken_effects": "<integer>",
    "changed_effect_threshold": "<integer>",
    "adjusted_tested_significant_terms": "<integer>",
    "raw_genome_significant_terms": "<integer>",
    "shared_significant_terms": "<integer>"
  }
]
```
- genes_fitted: integer (genes or terms); count under the specified analysis rules.
- raw_significant: integer (genes or terms); count under the specified analysis rules.
- adjusted_significant: integer (genes or terms); count under the specified analysis rules.
- large_shrunken_effects: integer (genes or terms); count under the specified analysis rules.
- changed_effect_threshold: integer (genes or terms); count under the specified analysis rules.
- adjusted_tested_significant_terms: integer (genes or terms); count under the specified analysis rules.
- raw_genome_significant_terms: integer (genes or terms); count under the specified analysis rules.
- shared_significant_terms: integer (genes or terms); count under the specified analysis rules.
Numeric tolerance is abs(actual - reference) <= atol + rtol * abs(reference).
Also write /app/sample_qc.tsv as UTF-8 TSV, with an id column and exactly these columns: library_counts, detected_genes, size_factor.
